items.key: ai:mysuru dasara 2026: the story of nishane aane, the elephant that leads jamboo savari
items.text: Mysuru Dasara 2026: The Story Of Nishane Aane, The Elephant That Leads Jamboo Savari
items.article: Carrying the royal insignia, the Nishane elephant proceeds to a designated point and receives a ceremonial salute. When the grand Jamboo Savari procession winds its way through the streets of Mysuru, thousands of spectators eagerly await one iconic sight: the elephant carrying the glittering golden howdah, or Ambari. It is the defining image of Mysuru Dasara, captured in photographs and celebrated year after year. But before the Ambari elephant makes its appearance, another elephant has already taken the lead. Carrying a flag bearing the royal insignia , it walks at the head of the procession, surrounded by drum beats, musical performances, cultural troupes and cheering crowds. This is the ‘Nishane Aane’, the ceremonial leader of the Jamboo Savari . The term ‘Nishane’ refers to a sign or signal marking the beginning of an event or procession. In the Jamboo Savari, the flag-bearing elephant plays this ceremonial role, announcing the commencement of the grand procession. Carrying the royal insignia, the Nishane elephant proceeds to a designated point and receives a ceremonial salute. This marks the formal beginning of the Jamboo Savari, one of the central attractions of Mysuru Dasara . The Nishane elephant is, therefore, more than just the first elephant in the procession. It holds a distinct ceremonial responsibility, signalling the start of a tradition that draws large crowds to Mysuru every year.

items.article: Slaven Bilic will not have the full backing of the Croatia supporters for his homecoming England take on Croatia this weekend, in a rematch from a six-goal thriller nearly four months ago at the World Cup. Thomas Tuchel's side travel to the Stadion HNK Rijeka looking to follow up their win over Czech Republic which kick-started their 2026/27 Nations League campaign. The Three Lions boss will be able to call upon Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham, two scorers in Dallas when England beat Croatia 4-2 back in June , as well as the likes of Alex Scott and the in-form Anthony Gordon. But their second successive away match in the competition is to be, mostly, played behind closed doors. The partial ban on supporters attending is part of a punishment handed down to Croatia regarding sanctions that date back to March 2025 and incidents involving fans around matches against France in the quarter-finals of the Nations League. Croatia's football association paid a fine of around £80,000 and faced disciplinary proceedings relating to racism and discrimination.

items.text: What happens to items confiscated at airport security? From baseball bats to whisky decanters, we pull back the curtain on the surprising afterlife of surrendered belongings
items.article: Sad to part ways with your above-limit expensive shampoo or nail scissors? Here's what really happens to your confiscated items... Published: 12:08, 2 October 2026 | Updated: 12:12, 2 October 2026 We all know that frustrating moment when, after sailing through security at the airport, your bag is hauled aside for an extra check. Whether it's a pair of nail scissors, a razor or an extra power bank that has you receiving that oh-so-judgemental look from security personnel, it's always frustrating to have your belongings confiscated before jetting off on holiday. But what actually happens to your items once they've been confiscated? Earlier this year, Manchester Airport showcased a selection of items its security officers were forced to confiscate in the space of just one morning. Among almost 100 items removed from bags in Terminal 2 security in July were 24 packs of cosmetic products, seven drinks bottles and seven food items – including two multipacks of yoghurts.

items.text: Aggressive bowel cancer that kills half of patients rising in TEENS - 5 signs often missed including back pain
items.article: CASES of aggressive bowel cancer that kills half of those it strikes are rising in teens and young adults, scientists warn. As the disease... CASES of aggressive bowel cancer that kills half of those it strikes are rising in teens and young adults, scientists warn. As the disease historically affects older adults, youngsters may be missing warning signs – which include tummy aches and lower back pain. Researchers from Mass General Brigham for Children and Mass General Brigham Cancer Institute found that children and teens with bowel cancer face “extreme delays” in diagnosis. As a result, many won’t be diagnosed with cancer until it’s reached an advanced stage – making treatment trickier and increasing the likelihood of death. items.article: FOR the millions of Brits with ADHD, a daily stimulant tablet holds the potential to unlock a new world - one that is quieter, less chaotic, with a... FOR the millions of Brits with ADHD, a daily stimulant tablet holds the potential to unlock a new world – one that is quieter, less chaotic, with a level playing field. The surge in prescription drugs for ADHD has been explosive in the past few years. But for some, it’s not all it’s cracked up to be. Others are spooked by little-known risks on the heart and even death, leaving them searching more desperately for answers to manage symptoms. When Michelle Akpata, 30, was diagnosed with ADHD, she hoped a prescription from her GP would rid her of the extra load she’d been carrying for years. “It often felt like running a marathon mentally just to stay organised throughout the day,” says Michelle, a broadcaster and radio presenter from London . “I realised that my difficulty maintaining focus and structure wasn’t just stress, but a consistent pattern affecting my day-to-day life.” But after starting Ritalin (10mg), the initial surge in energy gave way to troubling side effects.
